newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends off, bearish inventory data seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends off, bearish inventory data seen.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil lost ground Tuesday on expectations that weekly oil inventory data to be released this evening will show a bearish build in distillate stocks.
"Heating oil fell ahead of the stats," said a trader.

January heating oil settled off 1.28 cents a gallon at 73.54 cents after rising to a contract high Monday on forecasts of a cold spell in many U.S. regions. But, on Tuesday, Weather Services Corp said temperatures expected to hit the East Coast will not be as cold as they will be in the Midwest, hurting heating oil prices, dealers said.
The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.

A Reuters average of trader estimates for the oil stock data compiled by the American Petroleum Institute shows distillate stocks building by about 500,000 barrels for the week ended December 13. Distillate stocks are comprised of heating oil and diesel.
Heating oil's losses weighed on crude, with January crude ending off three cents a barrel at $25.71.
Due to some gasoline supply disruption, January gasoline bucked declines to end up 0.25 cent at 69.77 cents a gallon.
Exxon said a 102,000 barrel per day gasoline making unit at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana refinery would be shut for a few days for repair.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
